note: Both sets draw on the same wiring-schedule rows and every value is correctly bound: 151 (AL 3#4/0, armored cable), 150 (AL 3#4/0, #4G, 2-1/2"C), 50 (CU 3#6, #8G, 1"C), 34 (CU 6#10, 3#10G, 1"C), 33 (CU 6#10, #10G, 1"C), 32 (CU 2#10USE-2), 31 (CU 2#10, #10G, 3/4"C), 20 (CU 3#12, #12G, 3/4"C), 10 (CU #12/2WG). The two sets are content-identical (25 claims each, same facts, same quotes); the only difference is that B adds a spurious 'conditions: C.' to three conduit-size claims, where 'C.' is merely the abbreviation for conduit in the schedule, not a condition. Both sets omit the same facts (ground conductors for 20/31/50, the 2#10 conductors of 31, the #12/2WG of 10, the 'ARMORED CABLE' type of 151, and the NOTES panel ratings), so neither gains an advantage on coverage.
remarks: Text layer is jumbled (row order scrambled) but the image schedule is legible and consistent with it. Both sets append 'AWG' to '#6' and '#12' values that appear without a unit in the source — a mild unit inference, applied identically so it does not affect the comparison. Both sets leave out engineering facts present on the page: ground conductors (#12G for 20, #10G for 31, #8G for 50), the 2#10 conductors of 31, the #12/2WG of 10, 'ARMORED CABLE' for 151, and the NOTES entries (MAIN PANEL MP 120/240V 1Ø 3W, 150A/2P main breaker with main bonding jumper, 200A/2P NFDS NEMA 3R enclosure) plus the '4 AWG, COPPER TO GND' and 'L1, L2, & N, NO GND' interface notes. B's 'conditions: C.' pattern looks like a systematic mis-mapping of the conduit abbreviation into the conditions field.
